content.value_statement: Teams often struggle to keep features consistent across web, mobile, and desktop releases. This skill guides API-first planning, parallel implementation, and shared validation across platforms.
actual_capabilities: Guides API contract design before platform implementation begins.
Defines cross-platform design system requirements for web, iOS, Android, and desktop.
Plans shared business logic, state management, caching, and platform adapters.
Structures parallel implementation prompts for React, SwiftUI, Kotlin Compose, and desktop shells.
Creates validation steps for feature parity, accessibility, performance, and documentation.
limitations: It is a workflow guide and does not provide executable build scripts.
Generated plans depend on the user's feature requirements and existing architecture.
Platform code still needs human review, testing, and release approval.
Desktop file access and auto-update guidance must be scoped to the application need.

use_cases.title: Coordinate a Shared Feature Launch
use_cases.description: Plan one feature across web, iOS, Android, and desktop with common contracts and platform-specific tasks.

use_cases.title: Create Platform Implementation Prompts
use_cases.description: Turn a feature brief into focused prompts for frontend, mobile, backend, documentation, and testing work.

use_cases.title: Audit Cross-Platform Parity
use_cases.description: Build a validation matrix for behavior, accessibility, performance, documentation, and release readiness.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Feature Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to plan a multi-platform feature for web, iOS, Android, and desktop. Start with the API contract and list required decisions.

prompt_templates.title: Design Shared Architecture
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to define shared models, state management, caching, error handling, and platform adapters for this feature: [feature brief].

prompt_templates.title: Generate Platform Workstreams
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to split this feature into web, iOS, Android, desktop, documentation, testing, and optimization workstreams: [feature brief].

prompt_templates.title: Validate Release Parity
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to create a cross-platform validation plan covering parity, accessibility, performance, offline behavior, documentation, and store readiness.

output_examples.input: Plan a saved-search feature for web, iOS, Android, and desktop.
output_examples.output: A phased delivery plan with API contracts, shared models, platform workstreams, testing checkpoints, and release considerations.

output_examples.input: Review whether a mobile and web checkout flow have feature parity.
output_examples.output: A comparison matrix covering behavior, UI states, accessibility, error handling, offline cases, and performance targets.

output_examples.input: Prepare prompts for platform teams to implement a notifications feature.
output_examples.output: Separate prompts for backend, design, web, iOS, Android, desktop, documentation, testing, and optimization tasks.

best_practices: Define API contracts, shared models, and error formats before assigning platform work.
Use platform-native interface patterns while preserving common feature behavior.
Validate parity with a shared test matrix before release approval.
anti_patterns: Starting each platform from separate assumptions without a shared contract.
Forcing identical UI patterns where native platform behavior is expected.
Skipping accessibility, performance, and offline validation until late release stages.

faq.question: Does this skill generate complete applications?
faq.answer: No. It provides a structured workflow and prompts for planning, implementation, testing, and release coordination.

faq.question: Which platforms does it cover?
faq.answer: It covers web, iOS, Android, and optional desktop applications using Electron or Tauri.

faq.question: Can it work with existing APIs?
faq.answer: Yes. Provide the current API contract, and use the skill to align platform work around it.

faq.question: Does it require one shared codebase?
faq.answer: No. It can guide shared logic where useful while keeping platform-native implementations.

faq.question: Is this only for new features?
faq.answer: No. It can also structure parity reviews, migration planning, and platform gap analysis.

faq.question: Can Claude, Codex, or Claude Code use it?
faq.answer: Yes. The workflow is written for AI-assisted planning and implementation across supported coding agents.
